sentences.text:
Through: Mr. Sanjay Kumar Pathak with
 Mr. Sunil Kumar Jha, Mr. M. S.
 Akhtar, Ms. Rini V. Tigga, Mr.
 Piyush Pathak and Ms. Nidhi Thaku
 Advs. for R-1 to R-3
 Ms. Shobhana Takiar, Standing
 Counsel, Dda
 Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice V. Kameswar Rao
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Anoop Kumar Mendiratta
 Order

We have heard Mr. A.S. Chandhiok, learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner, Mr. Sanjay Kumar Pathak, learned counsel for respondent Nos.1, 2 and 3 and Ms. Shobhana Takiar, learned counsel for respondent No.4.
2.
This is a second round of litigation initiated by petitioner.

The earlier one being W.P.(C)
2299/2002, which was filed challenging notifications issued under Section 4, 6 and 17 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and also the award dated December 9, 2022.
The writ petition was finally decided by this Court vide order dated November 13, 2014.
3. During the pendency of the writ petition, as the Act of 2013 was notified, a CM APPL. 7190/2014 was filed by the petitioner.

Vide order dated November 13, 2014, this Court had allowed, both, the writ petition and the application, as is clear from paragraph 13 of the order dated November 13,
Santosh Singh vs Government Of Nct Of Delhi & Ors on 11 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42786272/
1 2014 which we reproduce as under:-
"13.

entities.text: Santosh Singh vs Government Of Nct Of Delhi & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above discussion, this Court is of the opinion that the application and the writ petition have to be allowed.

It is hereby declared that the land acquisition proceedings in relation to the suit lands under the old Act are deemed to have lapsed pursuant to coming into force of Section 24 of the new LA Act."
4.
The order dated November 13, 2014 became subject matter of two SLPs filed by the respondent Nos.1 to 3 and DDA.

The SLP filed by the respondent Nos.1 to 3 was decided by the Supreme Court in terms of order dated February 08, 2018 whereby the order dated November 13, 2014 was set aside, on the ground the question that acquisition has lapsed under Section 24 of the Act, 2013 has been decided by the Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No. 20982/2017, Indore Development Authority v. Shailendra (Dead) Thr. LR's.
5.

entities.text: Indore Development Authority v. Shailendra (Dead) Thr. LR
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The SLP filed by the DDA was also decided vide order dated February 20, 2018 whereby the only ground raised on behalf of the petitioner herein with reference to Section 5A was not accepted and the order was set aside.

6. The submission of Mr. Chandhiok with regard to filing of the present petition is that though the Supreme Court in its judgment of February 08, 2014 has stated that operation of stay in favour of the petitioner, cannot be a ground to take recourse to Section 24(2) of the Act of 2013, but after passing of the judgment on February 08, 2018, the fact that the respondents have not taken the possession nor paid compensation, the benefit of Section 24(2) shall accrue to the petitioner, now.

7. Mr. Pathak, learned counsel for respondent Nos.1 to 3 would contest the very maintainability of the petition on the ground that the acquisition having been upheld and the benefit of Section 24 (2)
of the Act of 2013 was not available to the petitioner, in view of the fact that the Supreme Court has set aside the judgment of this Court of November 13, 2014, the present petition shall be hit by the principle of res judicata.
That apart, he contends that on the ground of delay and latches also the present petition shall not be maintainable.

8. On a query to Ms. Shobhana Takiar and Mr. Pathak, whether the possession of the total area acquired through the notification issued under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 has been taken and compensation has been paid / deposited, they state they have to take instructions.
9. If that be so, appropriate shall be, for this Court to issue notice.

Mr. Sanjay Kumar Pathak,
accepts notice for respondent Nos.1, 2 and 3.

Ms. Shobhana Takiar, accepts notice for respondent No.4.
10.
Counter affidavit be filed within three weeks.
Rejoinder thereto be filed within two weeks thereafter.

11. Noting the said submission, we deem it appropriate to direct maintenance of status quo as of today with regard to land comprising of Khasra Nos.29/6/2, 7/2, 180/2, 29/6/3, 7/3, 14 and 15,
Santosh Singh vs Government Of Nct Of Delhi & Ors on 11 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42786272/
2 Revenue Estate of Village Pochanpur Tehsil Mehrauli, Delhi till the next date of hearing.
12. List on July 11, 2023.
